card.title: ME BF 110 E
card.text: Deployment: Gets Blitz if you control the frontline.
card.flavorText: The Bf 110 E Zerstörer 4 was a variant of the Messerschmitt Bf 110 twin-engine heavy fighter aircraft used by the Luftwaffe during WWII. It was a development of the Bf 110C variant and was introduced into service in 1941. The Bf 110E Zerstörer 4 was designed as a long-range fighter-bomber, capable of engaging both ground targets and enemy aircraft. It was armed with two 20mm MG FF/M cannon and four 7.92mm MG 17 machine guns, and up to 1,200 kg (2,650 lb) bombload. The Bf 110 E was powered by two Daimler-Benz DB 601 engines which allowed the aircraft to achieve a top speed of around 560 km/h (348 mph) at 6,000 meters (19,685 feet) altitude. One of the main differences between the Bf 110 E series and earlier Bf 110 variants was the improved armor protection for the pilot and crew, as well as for the engines and fuel tanks. The aircraft also had an improved cockpit layout, which provided better visibility for the pilot. The Bf 110 E was used extensively in the ground-attack role, particularly in the Eastern Front where it was used to attack Soviet armored columns and ground targets. It was also used for long-range fighter missions, including bomber escort duties. Overall, the Bf 110 was a versatile and capable aircraft that played an important role in the Luftwaffe's arsenal during WWII. Its combination of heavy firepower and long range made it a formidable opponent for both ground and air targets, and it is still considered an iconic aircraft of the war.
